11	// TrivyReport represents the JSON output from Trivy
12	type TrivyReport struct {
13		Results []TrivyResult `json:"Results"`
14	}
15	
16	// TrivyResult represents a single result from Trivy
17	type TrivyResult struct {
18		Target            string                  `json:"Target"`
19		Class             string                  `json:"Class"`
20		Type              string                  `json:"Type"`
21		Vulnerabilities   []TrivyVulnerability    `json:"Vulnerabilities"`
22		Secrets           []TrivySecret           `json:"Secrets,omitempty"`
23		Licenses          []TrivyLicense          `json:"Licenses,omitempty"`
24		Misconfigurations []TrivyMisconfiguration `json:"Misconfigurations,omitempty"`
25	}

27	// TrivyVulnerability represents a vulnerability found by Trivy
28	type TrivyVulnerability struct {
29		VulnerabilityID  string   `json:"VulnerabilityID"`
30		PkgName          string   `json:"PkgName"`
31		InstalledVersion string   `json:"InstalledVersion"`
32		FixedVersion     string   `json:"FixedVersion"`
33		Severity         string   `json:"Severity"`
34		Title            string   `json:"Title"`
35		Description      string   `json:"Description"`
36		PrimaryURL       string   `json:"PrimaryURL,omitempty"`
37		References       []string `json:"References,omitempty"`
38	}

41	type TrivySecret struct {
42		RuleID    string `json:"RuleID"`
43		Category  string `json:"Category"`
44		Severity  string `json:"Severity"`
45		Title     string `json:"Title"`
46		StartLine int    `json:"StartLine"`

49	}

52	type TrivyLicense struct {
53		Severity   string  `json:"Severity"`
54		Category   string  `json:"Category"` // forbidden, restricted, reciprocal, notice, permissive, unencumbered, unknown
55		PkgName    string  `json:"PkgName"`
56		FilePath   string  `json:"FilePath"`
57		Name       string  `json:"Name"` // License identifier (SPDX): MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0, etc.
58		Confidence float64 `json:"Confidence"`

60	}

63	type TrivyMisconfiguration struct {
64		Type          string `json:"Type"`
65		ID            string `json:"ID"`
66		AVDID         string `json:"AVDID"`
67		Title         string `json:"Title"`

77		} `json:"CauseMetadata"`

80	// RunTrivy executes Trivy and returns findings.
81	// progressFn is an optional callback called with each stderr line (DB download progress etc.).
82	func RunTrivy(ctx context.Context, target string, targetType TargetType, licenseMode bool, tool ToolSpec, server string, ignoreUnfixed bool, ignoreEOL bool, progressFn func(string)) ([]Finding, error) {
83		tc, err := trivyArgs(target, targetType, licenseMode, tool, server, ignoreUnfixed, ignoreEOL)
84		if err != nil {
85			return nil, err
86		}
87		return runTrivy(ctx, tc, progressFn)
88	}
89	
90	// trivySem serializes every Trivy process this application starts.
91	//
92	// Trivy's local cache — the vulnerability database and the fs cache, both
93	// BoltDB — allows only one writer at a time. Scanner.Scan starts several
94	// Trivy stages concurrently for a single target (vuln, secret, misconfig),
95	// and a batch scan runs several targets concurrently on top of that: two
96	// Trivy processes racing for the cache lock do not queue behind each other,
97	// the loser fails outright with "unable to acquire cache or database lock".
98	// A size-1 semaphore around every invocation turns that race into a queue.
99	var trivySem = make(chan struct{}, 1)
100	
101	// runTrivy executes a built invocation and parses what it wrote to stdout.
102	//
103	// A non-zero exit is not on its own a failure: Trivy exits 1 when it finds
104	// vulnerabilities, and the report on stdout is exactly what the caller asked
105	// for. Only an exit that produced no report is reported as an error.
106	func runTrivy(ctx context.Context, tc toolCmd, progressFn func(string)) ([]Finding, error) {
107		select {
108		case trivySem <- struct{}{}:
109		case <-ctx.Done():
110			return nil, ctx.Err()
111		}
112		defer func() { <-trivySem }()
113	
114		stdout, err := runner.Run(ctx, tc, progressFn)
115		if err != nil {
116			var exit *exitError
117			if !errors.As(err, &exit) || len(stdout) == 0 {
118				return nil, fmt.Errorf("trivy failed: %w", err)
119			}
120		}
121		return parseTrivyOutput(stdout)
122	}
123	
124	// trivyFixCommand is the command that clears a vulnerability, or, for an
125	// ecosystem with no known command, the plain instruction the finding always
126	// carried. Empty when Trivy knows of no fixed version.
127	func trivyFixCommand(ecosystem string, vuln TrivyVulnerability) string {
128		target := PickFixed(vuln.InstalledVersion, vuln.FixedVersion)
129		if target == "" {
130			if vuln.FixedVersion == "" {
131				return ""
132			}
133			target = vuln.FixedVersion
134		}
135		if cmd, ok := FixCommand(ecosystem, vuln.PkgName, target); ok {
136			return cmd
137		}
138		return fmt.Sprintf("Update %s to %s", vuln.PkgName, target)
139	}
140	
141	// parseTrivyOutput parses Trivy JSON output into findings
142	func parseTrivyOutput(data []byte) ([]Finding, error) {
143		var report TrivyReport
144		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &report); err != nil {
145			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse trivy output: %w", err)
146		}
147	
148		var findings []Finding
149	
150		for _, result := range report.Results {
151			// Process vulnerabilities
152			for _, vuln := range result.Vulnerabilities {
153				// Build references from PrimaryURL and advisory links
154				refs := make([]string, 0, len(vuln.References)+1)
155				if vuln.PrimaryURL != "" {
156					refs = append(refs, vuln.PrimaryURL)
157				}
158				for _, r := range vuln.References {
159					if r != vuln.PrimaryURL {
160						refs = append(refs, r)
161					}
162				}
163	
164				// Build a fix command suggestion when a fixed version is known
165				fixCmd := trivyFixCommand(result.Type, vuln)
166	
167				findings = append(findings, Finding{
168					ID:          vuln.VulnerabilityID,
169					Title:       vuln.Title,
170					Description: vuln.Description,
171					Severity:    parseSeverity(vuln.Severity),
172					Source:      "trivy",
173					File:        result.Target,
174					PkgName:     vuln.PkgName,
175					Version:     vuln.InstalledVersion,
176					FixedIn:     vuln.FixedVersion,
177					Class:       result.Class,
178					Ecosystem:   result.Type,
179					References:  refs,
180					FixCommand:  fixCmd,
181				})
182			}
183	
184			// Process secrets found by Trivy.
185			//
186			// The report has carried these since TrivySecret was declared; nothing
187			// read them, so a secret Trivy found was parsed and dropped. Only the
188			// secret stage asks for them (--scanners secret), so there is no risk of
189			// the vulnerability stage returning the same finding twice.
190			for _, secret := range result.Secrets {
191				findings = append(findings, Finding{
192					ID:          secret.RuleID,
193					Title:       secret.Title,
194					Description: secret.Category,
195					Severity:    parseSeverity(secret.Severity),
196					Source:      SourceTrivySecret,
197					File:        result.Target,
198					Line:        secret.StartLine,
199					Match:       maskSecret(secret.Match),
200				})
201			}
202	
203			// Process licenses found by Trivy
204			for _, license := range result.Licenses {
205				findings = append(findings, Finding{
206					ID:          license.Name,
207					Title:       fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", license.PkgName, license.Name),
208					Description: fmt.Sprintf("License category: %s", license.Category),
209					Severity:    parseSeverity(license.Severity),
210					Source:      "trivy-license",
211					File:        license.FilePath,
212					PkgName:     license.PkgName,
213				})
214			}
215	
216			// Process misconfigurations found by Trivy
217			for _, misconf := range result.Misconfigurations {
218				var miscRefs []string
219				if misconf.PrimaryURL != "" {
220					miscRefs = append(miscRefs, misconf.PrimaryURL)
221				}
222				findings = append(findings, Finding{
223					ID:          firstNonEmpty(misconf.AVDID, misconf.ID),
224					Title:       misconf.Title,
225					Description: misconf.Desc,
226					Severity:    parseSeverity(misconf.Severity),
227					Source:      "trivy-misconfig",
228					File:        result.Target,
229					Line:        misconf.CauseMetadata.StartLine,
230					EndLine:     misconf.CauseMetadata.EndLine,
231					Message:     misconf.Message,
232					Status:      misconf.Status,
233					Resolution:  misconf.Resolution,
234					References:  miscRefs,
235				})
236			}
237		}
238	
239		return findings, nil
240	}

242	// parseSeverity converts string severity to SeverityLevel
243	func parseSeverity(s string) SeverityLevel {
244		switch strings.ToUpper(s) {
245		case "CRITICAL":
246			return SeverityCritical
247		case "HIGH":
248			return SeverityHigh
249		case "MEDIUM":
250			return SeverityMedium
251		case "LOW":
252			return SeverityLow
253		default:
254			return SeverityUnknown
255		}
256	}

258	// firstNonEmpty returns the first non-empty value, or "" if all are empty.
259	//

261	// and leave AVDID blank, so falling back to it is what keeps the remediation
262	// catalog's lookup (which matches on Finding.ID) working across those reports.
263	func firstNonEmpty(values ...string) string {
264		for _, v := range values {
265			if v != "" {
266				return v
267			}
268		}
269		return ""
270	}

272	// maskSecret partially masks secret values for display
273	func maskSecret(s string) string {
274		if len(s) <= 8 {
275			return "****"
276		}
277		return s[:4] + "****" + s[len(s)-4:]
278	}

253		r.MisconfigCount = 0

263			case CategoryCIScore:

377	// CheckDependencies works out where each scanner runs from, for one context's
378	// scan configuration.
379	//
380	// It replaces CheckDependenciesWithImages, which took only the two image names.
381	// That signature is why `trivy_path` and `gitleaks_path` were never read: there
382	// was nowhere to pass them (D27). Taking the whole ScanConfig also lets the
383	// per-tool source preference be honoured, which binary-first resolution made
384	// impossible to express.
385	func CheckDependencies(c config.ScanConfig) DependencyStatus {
386		trivyImage := c.TrivyImage
387		if trivyImage == "" {
388			trivyImage = DefaultTrivyImage
389		}
390		gitleaksImage := c.GitleaksImage
391		if gitleaksImage == "" {
392			gitleaksImage = DefaultGitleaksImage
393		}
394		plumberImage := c.PlumberImage
395		if plumberImage == "" {
396			plumberImage = DefaultPlumberImage
397		}
398	
399		status := DependencyStatus{
400			TrivySource:    ToolSourceNone,
401			TrivyImage:     trivyImage,
402			GitleaksSource: ToolSourceNone,
403			GitleaksImage:  gitleaksImage,
404			PlumberSource:  ToolSourceNone,
405			PlumberImage:   plumberImage,
406		}
407	
408		if path, err := exec.LookPath(engine.Current().Binary); err == nil && path != "" {
409			status.EngineAvailable = true
410			status.ImageScanSocket = engine.Current().HostSocket()
411		}
412	
413		trivy := resolveTool(c.TrivySource, c.TrivyPath, "trivy", trivyImage, status.EngineAvailable, "--version")
414		status.TrivyAvailable = trivy.Available
415		status.TrivySource = trivy.Source
416		status.TrivyBinary = trivy.Binary
417		status.TrivyVersion = trivy.Version
418	
419		gitleaks := resolveTool(c.GitleaksSource, c.GitleaksPath, "gitleaks", gitleaksImage, status.EngineAvailable, "version")
420		status.GitleaksAvailable = gitleaks.Available
421		status.GitleaksSource = gitleaks.Source
422		status.GitleaksBinary = gitleaks.Binary
423		status.GitleaksVersion = gitleaks.Version
424	
425		// `plumber version` writes the installed version to stdout and an upgrade
426		// notice — "plumber v0.4.44 is available (you have 0.4.40)" — to stderr.
427		// toolVersion reads stdout only, so the two cannot be confused; measured
428		// rather than assumed, because reporting the available version as the
429		// installed one is the kind of thing nobody notices for months.
430		plumber := resolveTool(c.PlumberSource, c.PlumberPath, "plumber", plumberImage, status.EngineAvailable, "version")
431		status.PlumberAvailable = plumber.Available
432		status.PlumberSource = plumber.Source
433		status.PlumberBinary = plumber.Binary
434		status.PlumberVersion = plumber.Version
435	
436		return status
437	}

544	// Scan performs a security scan on the target, running all enabled stages in parallel.
545	func (s *Scanner) Scan(ctx context.Context, target string, targetType TargetType) (*Result, error) {
546		result := &Result{
547			Target:     target,
548			TargetType: targetType,
549			StartTime:  time.Now(),
550			Findings:   []Finding{},
551			Errors:     []string{},
552		}
553	
554		notify := func(update ProgressUpdate) {
555			if s.options.OnProgress != nil {
556				s.options.OnProgress(update)
557			}
558		}
559	
560		// A stage whose tool is missing is not started at all, so it leaves neither a
561		// finding nor an error behind — and a result with neither is indistinguishable
562		// from a clean scan. Recording the reason up front is what stops "nothing
563		// looked at this image" being reported as "this image is fine" (§1.3 D20).
564		result.Errors = append(result.Errors, s.missingToolErrors(targetType)...)
565	
566		// mu guards writes to result (Findings, Errors) from concurrent goroutines
567		var mu sync.Mutex
568	
569		eg, egCtx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx)
570	
571		// Vuln scan (Trivy)
572		if s.options.EnableVuln && s.deps.TrivyAvailable {
573			eg.Go(func() error {
574				notify(ProgressUpdate{Stage: "vuln", Label: "Vulnerabilities", Status: StageRunning})
575				progressFn := func(detail string) {
576					notify(ProgressUpdate{Stage: "vuln", Label: "Vulnerabilities", Status: StageRunning, Detail: detail})
577				}
578				cmd := GetTrivyCommand(target, targetType, false, s.deps.TrivySpec(), s.options.TrivyServer, s.options.IgnoreUnfixed, s.options.IgnoreEOL)
579				log.Printf("Running: %s", cmd)
580				findings, err := RunTrivy(egCtx, target, targetType, false, s.deps.TrivySpec(), s.options.TrivyServer, s.options.IgnoreUnfixed, s.options.IgnoreEOL, progressFn)
581				mu.Lock()
582				defer mu.Unlock()
583				if err != nil {
584					recordStageError(result, "trivy vuln", err)
585					notify(ProgressUpdate{Stage: "vuln", Label: "Vulnerabilities", Status: StageError, Detail: err.Error()})
586				} else {
587					result.Findings = append(result.Findings, findings...)
588					notify(ProgressUpdate{Stage: "vuln", Label: "Vulnerabilities", Status: StageDone})
589				}
590				return nil
591			})
592		}
593	
594		// License scan (Trivy, directory only)
595		if s.options.EnableLicense && s.deps.TrivyAvailable && targetType == TargetDirectory {
596			eg.Go(func() error {

13	// toolCmd is one subprocess invocation: the binary and the arguments handed to
14	// it. Building it is pure, which is what makes the argument surface — the part
15	// that decides what a scanner is actually asked to do — testable without a
16	// scanner installed.
17	//
18	// It is also what the UI displays. Deriving the shown command and the executed
19	// one from the same value is the point: the two used to be built separately and
20	// had drifted (§1.3 D19).
21	type toolCmd struct {
22		Name string
23		Args []string
24		// Env is the child's whole environment when it is not nil, os.Environ()
25		// plus what the caller added. It exists so a credential can reach a tool
26		// without going through argv, which is readable from the process list —
27		// the arrangement the clone already uses for http.extraHeader (§3.16).
28		//
29		// String() never renders it: the invocation is logged and shown in the UI.
30		Env []string
31	
32		// Dir is the working directory the tool runs in, when it has one.
33		//
34		// It exists for plumber, whose `analyze` takes **no path argument**: it
35		// works on the current directory. Without this the tool ran in whatever
36		// directory DevDesk was launched from and reported
37		// `--project is required (could not auto-detect from git remote)` — a
38		// failure about a repository nobody had asked it to look at. Trivy and
39		// Gitleaks take their target in argv and set nothing here.
40		Dir string
41	}

43	// String renders the invocation as a shell command line, for logs and for the
44	// command the UI shows next to a scan.
45	func (c toolCmd) String() string {
46		if c.Name == "" {
47			return ""
48		}
49		line := strings.Join(append([]string{c.Name}, c.Args...), " ")
50		// The directory is part of what the command means when the tool takes no
51		// path: a logged invocation that cannot be re-run says less than it looks
52		// like it does.
53		if c.Dir != "" {
54			return "cd " + c.Dir + " && " + line
55		}
56		return line
57	}

59	// exitError reports a tool that ran and exited non-zero. The code matters:
60	// both scanners use a non-zero exit to mean "I found something" rather than
61	// "I failed" — trivy for vulnerabilities, gitleaks for secrets — so callers
62	// have to tell the two apart.
63	type exitError struct {
64		Code   int
65		Stderr string
66	}
67	
68	func (e *exitError) Error() string {
69		if e.Stderr != "" {
70			return fmt.Sprintf("exit status %d: %s", e.Code, strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr))
71		}
72		return fmt.Sprintf("exit status %d", e.Code)
73	}

75	// commandRunner is the seam every subprocess in this package passes through.
76	//
77	// The package drives trivy and gitleaks as external processes, which makes it
78	// untestable without both installed and a repository to point them at. Routing
79	// through this interface lets tests exercise the argument building, the
80	// exit-code handling and the output parsing — where the defects live — against
81	// canned output.
82	type commandRunner interface {
83		// Run executes tc and returns what it wrote to stdout. Lines written to
84		// stderr are forwarded to progressFn as they arrive, which is how Trivy
85		// reports its database download. A tool that runs and exits non-zero
86		// returns its stdout along with an *exitError.
87		Run(ctx context.Context, tc toolCmd, progressFn func(string)) ([]byte, error)
88	}
89	
90	// cliRunner is the production commandRunner: it shells out to the real tools.
91	type cliRunner struct{}
92	
93	func (cliRunner) Run(ctx context.Context, tc toolCmd, progressFn func(string)) ([]byte, error) {
94		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, tc.Name, tc.Args...) //nolint:gosec // name is one of trivy/gitleaks/plumber/docker
95		cmd.Env = tc.Env                                     // nil inherits this process's environment, which is the default
96		cmd.Dir = tc.Dir                                     // empty runs in DevDesk's own working directory
97	
98		var stdout bytes.Buffer
99		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
100	
101		// Stderr is consumed two ways: streamed to progressFn while the tool runs,
102		// and kept so a failure can be reported with the tool's own diagnostic.
103		var stderr bytes.Buffer
104		if progressFn != nil {
105			pipe, err := cmd.StderrPipe()
106			if err == nil {
107				done := make(chan struct{})
108				go func() {
109					defer close(done)
110					sc := bufio.NewScanner(pipe)
111					for sc.Scan() {
112						line := strings.TrimSpace(sc.Text())
113						if line == "" {
114							continue
115						}
116						stderr.WriteString(line)
117						stderr.WriteByte('\n')
118						progressFn(line)
119					}
120					// A read failure on the progress pipe is not a scan failure:
121					// the report comes back on stdout, and the tool's exit code
122					// says whether it succeeded. Dropping the rest of the progress
123					// is the whole consequence.
124					_ = sc.Err()
125				}()
126				if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
127					return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s failed to start: %w", tc.Name, err)
128				}
129				<-done // drain stderr before Wait closes the pipe
130				return finish(tc.Name, cmd, &stdout, &stderr)
131			}
132		}
133	
134		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
135		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
136			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s failed to start: %w", tc.Name, err)
137		}
138		return finish(tc.Name, cmd, &stdout, &stderr)
139	}
140	
141	// finish waits for the tool and only then reads what it wrote.
142	//
143	// The order is the point, and it is not a style preference: os/exec fills the
144	// output buffers from goroutines it owns, and only Wait guarantees they are
145	// done. Reading the buffer in the same expression as Wait — which is what
146	// `return stdout.Bytes(), waitErr(..., cmd.Wait(), ...)` does, since operands
147	// are evaluated before the call — snapshots it while it is still empty, and
148	// every scan comes back with no findings.
149	func finish(name string, cmd *exec.Cmd, stdout, stderr *bytes.Buffer) ([]byte, error) {
150		err := cmd.Wait()
151		return stdout.Bytes(), waitErr(name, err, stderr.String())
152	}
153	
154	// waitErr turns a non-zero exit into an *exitError carrying the code, and
155	// leaves anything else (a killed process, a broken pipe) as it is.
156	func waitErr(name string, err error, stderr string) error {
157		if err == nil {
158			return nil
159		}
160		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
161		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
162			if stderr == "" {
163				stderr = string(exitErr.Stderr)
164			}
165			return &exitError{Code: exitErr.ExitCode(), Stderr: stderr}
166		}
167		return fmt.Errorf("%s failed: %w", name, err)
168	}

171	// package stays safe to call concurrently; tests that swap it must not run in
172	// parallel.
173	var runner commandRunner = cliRunner{}

20	// Exit codes. Four, not three: `3` says the analysis ran on incomplete data and
21	// the score is withheld, and it is the one that matters most here — it maps
22	// exactly onto the `?` state of the CI column, without anyone having to read
23	// dataCollectionDegraded out of the JSON to find out.

26		plumberRuntimeError  = 2 // no token, bad config, unreachable host, no repository
27		plumberScoreWithheld = 3 // it ran, and says it cannot conclude

31	// container, on §3.50's model: the argument plumber sees is never the host path.
32	//
33	// The container root is free of everything except /plumber, the binary itself
34	// (checked on getplumber/plumber). The repository is mounted at
35	// containerScanPath, so no file of it can land beside this one.
36	const plumberConfigMount = "/plumber.yaml"

38	// plumberSafeDirectory is what lets a containerised plumber read the mounted
39	// repository at all.
40	//
41	// The image runs as uid 65532, so git refuses the mount with `fatal: detected
42	// dubious ownership in repository at '/scan'` and plumber answers *could not
43	// determine the provider: not in a git repository*. Passing it through the
44	// environment rather than a config file is what keeps the mount read-only and
45	// the user non-root; `--user` is not portable to Windows hosts. Measured, not
46	// deduced: `--provider` alone does **not** lift it.

49		"-e", "GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory",

53	// PlumberOptions is what one plumber run needs beyond the tool itself.

56		// from the remote: config.ForgeGitLab or config.ForgeGitHub.

72	// plumberArgs builds the invocation.

75	// than chosen: in a container `--output /dev/stdout` works, and for a native
76	// Windows binary it writes nothing at all — there is no such path. So the
77	// binary mode writes to a file the caller passes in and deletes.
78	//
79	// `--print=false` is what keeps stdout pure JSON: the human report and the
80	// score banner both go there otherwise. The tool's own logs go to stderr, which
81	// is where progressFn reads them.
82	func plumberArgs(target string, tool ToolSpec, opts PlumberOptions, outPath string) toolCmd {
83		docker := tool.Source == ToolSourceContainer

85		configFlag := opts.ConfigPath
86		if docker && opts.ConfigPath != "" {
87			configFlag = plumberConfigMount

90		options := []string{"analyze", "--score", "--print=false", "--output", outPath}
91		if opts.Provider != "" {

93		}
94		if opts.Branch != "" {
95			options = append(options, "--branch", opts.Branch)
96		}
97		if opts.GitLabURL != "" {
98			options = append(options, "--gitlab-url", opts.GitLabURL)
99		}
100		if opts.ConfigPath != "" {
101			options = append(options, "--config", configFlag)
102		}

104		if docker {
105			args := []string{"run", "--rm", "-v", target + ":" + containerScanPath + ":ro"}
106			if opts.ConfigPath != "" {
107				// Before the image name: everything after it is plumber's own argv.
108				args = append(args, "-v", opts.ConfigPath+":"+plumberConfigMount+":ro")

21	// ciOptions decides whether plumber runs on this target, and with what.
22	//
23	// It is resolved **per target, not per batch**: one batch holds repositories
24	// with different remotes and different branches, so a single set of options for
25	// all of them would grade the wrong thing — or grade a repository of another
26	// forge, which is the whole point of the rule.
27	//
28	// The remote is read here rather than passed in because this is the only place
29	// that needs it and the two views that start scans would otherwise each carry
30	// the rule. Reading it costs one `git` call per repository, and only when the
31	// setting is on.
32	func (s *Scanner) ciOptions(target string, targetType TargetType) (PlumberOptions, bool) {
33		// An image has no pipeline, so there is nothing to grade.
34		if !s.options.EnableCIScore || targetType != TargetDirectory || !s.deps.PlumberAvailable {
35			return PlumberOptions{}, false
36		}
37		status, err := git.ReadStatus(target)
38		if err != nil {
39			// Not a repository: not a failure of the scan, just nothing to grade.
40			return PlumberOptions{}, false
41		}
42		return ciOptionsFor(s.options, status.Remote, status.Branch, s.options.LoadForgeToken)
43	}

45	// ciOptionsFor is the rule itself, separated from the git read so a test can
46	// state it without a repository on disk.
47	func ciOptionsFor(o ScanOptions, remoteURL, branch string, loadToken func() string) (PlumberOptions, bool) {
48		if !git.SameHost(remoteURL, o.Forge.URL) {
49			return PlumberOptions{}, false
50		}
51	
52		opts := PlumberOptions{
53			Provider:   plumberProvider(o.Forge.Type),
54			Branch:     branch,

56		}

59		}
60		// Only the GitLab path takes an instance URL. Passing one on the GitHub
61		// path is what makes plumber choose the GitLab path — the flag is part of
62		// how it decides — so it would send a GitHub context to a GitLab it has no
63		// token for.

149	func (m *Model) filterFindingsByTab() []scan.Finding {
150		if m.result == nil {

154		want, ok := tabCategory[m.activeTab]

157		}

176		case scan.SourceTrivyMisconfig:

178		case scan.SourceGitleaks:

180		case scan.SourceTrivySecret:

182		case scan.SourceTrivy:

191	func (m *Model) countFindingsByTab() (cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci int) {

12	// A misconfiguration is not fixed the way a vulnerability is (§3.78). Trivy
13	// reports the block it faults and a Resolution written in English — a sentence,
14	// not a replacement — so there is no general way to turn one into an edit.
15	//
16	// What there is instead is a **deliberately finite** catalog: the few rules that
17	// recur often enough to be worth writing by hand, each with the exact edit that
18	// satisfies it. A rule absent from the catalog is not a gap to be filled. It is
19	// the case the MCP server already covers, by handing a calling agent the span,
20	// the wording and the file (phase A) and re-measuring afterwards.
21	//
22	// That boundary is the point, and it is why Fix declines instead of
23	// approximating: an absence sends the user to something that works, while a
24	// doubtful edit sends them to a diff they have to second-guess.
25	
26	// Rule is one misconfiguration this application knows how to fix on its own.
27	type Rule struct {
28		// AVDID is the rule's identity as Trivy reports it in Finding.ID. It is
29		// matched loosely — see ruleKey — because Trivy spells the same rule
30		// "AVD-DS-0002" in one field and "DS002" in another.
31		AVDID string
32		// Title is what the UI calls the fix. It says what the edit does, not what
33		// the rule forbids: the user is agreeing to a change, not reading an advisory.
34		Title string
35		// Fix returns the edits that satisfy the rule on content, or nil and a
36		// reason when this instance is not one the catalog handles.
37		//
38		// It never guesses. An instance it cannot read exactly is one it declines,
39		// and the reason is shown to the user as-is (Rule 129: English).
40		Fix func(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string)
41	}

180	// FixFor returns the catalog's rule for a finding, if it has one.
181	//
182	// It answers for misconfigurations only. A vulnerability, a secret or a licence
183	// reaching here is not an error — the tab is shared — it simply has no rule.
184	func FixFor(f scan.Finding) (Rule, bool) {
185		if scan.Categorize(f) != scan.CategoryMisconfiguration {
186			return Rule{}, false
187		}
188		r, ok := catalog[RuleKey(f.ID)]
189		return r, ok
190	}

192	// RuleKey reduces the spellings of one rule id to a single key.
193	//
194	// Trivy writes "AVD-DS-0002" in AVDID and "DS002" in ID, and which of the two
195	// reaches a Finding has changed before. Matching on either spelling costs one
196	// function; matching on one of them costs a catalog that silently stops firing
197	// the day the other is used.
198	func RuleKey(id string) string {
199		id = strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(id))
200		id = strings.TrimPrefix(id, "AVD-")
201		id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, "-", "")
202	
203		letters := strings.IndexFunc(id, func(r rune) bool { return r >= '0' && r <= '9' })
204		if letters <= 0 {
205			return id
206		}
207		prefix, digits := id[:letters], strings.TrimLeft(id[letters:], "0")
208		if digits == "" {
209			digits = "0"
210		}
211		return prefix + digits
212	}

214	// fixRootUser satisfies "specify at least 1 USER command" by creating an
215	// unprivileged account in the final stage and switching to it.
216	//
217	// **It creates the account rather than naming a uid.** A bare `USER 10001`
218	// switches to a uid that has no passwd entry: no name, no home, no shell. Much
219	// of what runs in a container asks the system who it is — anything calling
220	// getpwuid, a shell wanting $HOME, tools that write to a home directory — and
221	// all of it degrades in ways that surface later, at run time, far from this
222	// edit. `adduser` first, `USER appuser` after, is what `docker init` generates
223	// and what this now emits.
224	//
225	// **The flags are Debian's, so the base image has to be one.** The long options
226	// below belong to the Debian/Ubuntu `adduser`; busybox's, on Alpine, takes
227	// different ones (`-D`, `-H`, `-s /sbin/nologin`) and a distroless image has no
228	// shell to run either in. Guessing wrong produces a Dockerfile that fails at
229	// build, which is worse than offering nothing — so a base this cannot identify
230	// is declined, and the agent path (phase A) takes it.
231	//
232	// The block goes before the final stage's first CMD or ENTRYPOINT, which is
233	// where it has to be to apply to the process that runs — after it, it would
234	// change nothing. With neither, it goes at the end of the file.
235	//
236	// What it does not do is chown anything. A process that loses root may no longer
237	// be able to write where it used to, and no edit computed from the Dockerfile
238	// alone can know. That is a change the user reads in the diff and agrees to, and
239	// that the re-scan then confirms cleared the rule — it is not a claim that the
240	// image still works.

1	// Package patch edits a text file by byte range: it replaces what an edit
2	// covers and nothing else, so comments, line endings — CRLF included — and the
3	// absence of a final newline survive exactly.
4	//
5	// It knows nothing about what it is editing. It was written for the Dockerfiles
6	// of the base image remediation (§3.2), lived in internal/dockerfile, and never
7	// read a Dockerfile: it takes bytes and spans, which is why §3.78 moved it out
8	// rather than writing a second copy for misconfigurations.
9	//
10	// The three pieces are deliberately separate. Rewrite computes the new content,
11	// Diff is what a user is shown before agreeing to it, and WriteIfUnchanged puts
12	// it on disk only if the file still holds what the edit was computed from — so
13	// what gets written is always what was agreed to.
14	package patch
15	
16	import (
17		"bytes"
18		"errors"
19		"fmt"
20		"sort"
21		"strings"
22	)
23	
24	// Span is a range of bytes, End exclusive.
25	type Span struct{ Start, End int }
26	
27	// Edit replaces the bytes Span covers, and says what it expects to find there.
28	type Edit struct {
29		Span Span
30		// Old is the text the span held when the file was read. Rewrite refuses an
31		// edit whose span no longer holds it: an offset is only meaningful for the
32		// content it was measured on, and applying it to another would cut
33		// something else in half.
34		Old string
35		New string
36	}
37	
38	// ErrConflict is returned when two edits ask for different text in the same
39	// place, or in places that overlap.
40	var ErrConflict = errors.New("conflicting edits")
41	
42	// Rewrite applies edits to content and returns the result. It changes the bytes
43	// the edits cover and nothing else, so comments, line endings — CRLF included —
44	// and the absence of a final newline survive exactly.
45	//
46	// Two edits on the same span with the same text are one edit: two stages that
47	// share a base image through one ARG both point at its default. The same span
48	// with different text is a conflict, as is any overlap, and either is an error
49	// rather than a choice made on the caller's behalf.
50	func Rewrite(content []byte, edits []Edit) ([]byte, error) {
51		edits, err := normalize(content, edits)
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, err
54		}
55		var out bytes.Buffer
56		out.Grow(len(content))
57		at := 0
58		for _, e := range edits {
59			out.Write(content[at:e.Span.Start])
60			out.WriteString(e.New)

259			Errors:         result.Errors,

261			Findings:       []finding{},
262		}
263		// Root is the repository itself: a workspace scan is run on that directory,
264		// so a finding's file is relative to it. An image has no such anchor, which
265		// is the whole point of the distinction.
266		if kind == kindRepository {
267			out.Root = result.Target
268		}
269	
270		severities := normalisedSet(in.Severity, strings.ToUpper)
271		categories := normalisedSet(in.Category, strings.ToLower)
272	
273		kept := make([]scan.Finding, 0, len(result.Findings))
274		for _, f := range result.Findings {
275			if len(severities) > 0 {
276				if _, ok := severities[strings.ToUpper(string(f.Severity))]; !ok {
277					continue
278				}
279			}
280			if len(categories) > 0 {
281				if _, ok := categories[categoryName(scan.Categorize(f))]; !ok {
282					continue
283				}
284			}
285			kept = append(kept, f)
286		}
287		out.Matched = len(kept)
288	
289		offset, limit := page(in.Offset, in.Limit)
290		out.Offset = offset
291		if offset >= len(kept) {
292			return out
293		}
294		end := offset + limit
295		if end > len(kept) {
296			end = len(kept)
297		}
298		for _, f := range kept[offset:end] {
299			out.Findings = append(out.Findings, expose(f))
300		}
301		return out
302	}
303	
304	// page normalises what the caller asked for. A negative offset is a mistake, not
305	// a request to count from the end; an absent limit is the default and an
306	// oversized one is capped, because the cap protects the agent's own context and
307	// a caller cannot waive that on its behalf.
308	func page(offset, limit int) (int, int) {
309		if offset < 0 {
310			offset = 0
311		}
312		switch {
313		case limit <= 0:
314			limit = defaultFindingLimit
315		case limit > maxFindingLimit:
316			limit = maxFindingLimit
317		}
318		return offset, limit
319	}
320	
321	// expose is the one place a scan.Finding becomes something that leaves the
322	// process. It names every field it copies, so a field added to scan.Finding
323	// arrives here as an omission rather than as an exposure — the same argument the
324	// allow-list of tools makes.
325	func expose(f scan.Finding) finding {
326		return finding{
327			ID:          f.ID,
328			Title:       f.Title,
329			Description: f.Description,
330			Severity:    string(f.Severity),
331			Category:    categoryName(scan.Categorize(f)),
332			Source:      f.Source,
333			File:        f.File,
334			Line:        f.Line,
335			EndLine:     f.EndLine,
336			Message:     f.Message,
337			Status:      f.Status,
338			Fingerprint: f.Fingerprint,
339			PkgName:     f.PkgName,
340			Version:     f.Version,
341			FixedIn:     f.FixedIn,
342			Class:       f.Class,
343			Ecosystem:   f.Ecosystem,
344			Resolution:  f.Resolution,
345			References:  f.References,
346		}
347	}
348	
349	// categoryName is scan.Category as a word. The type is an int with no String
350	// method, so a conversion would yield a rune rather than a name — and the four
351	// values are a vocabulary an agent filters on, which makes them part of the
352	// tool's contract rather than an internal enum.
353	//
354	// The default is "vulnerability" for the reason Categorize's is: a source this
355	// does not know stays visible in the family that is looked at first, rather than
356	// disappearing into a name nothing filters for.
357	func categoryName(c scan.Category) string {
358		switch c {
359		case scan.CategorySecret:
360			return "secret"
361		case scan.CategoryLicense:
362			return "license"
363		case scan.CategoryMisconfiguration:
364			return "misconfiguration"
365		default:
366			return "vulnerability"
367		}
368	}
369	
370	func normalisedSet(values []string, normalise func(string) string) map[string]struct{} {
371		out := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
372		for _, v := range values {
373			if v = normalise(strings.TrimSpace(v)); v != "" {
374				out[v] = struct{}{}
375			}
376		}
377		return out
378	}

29		// **always** written (`json:"sensitive"`, without omitempty), so a file
30		// written by a previous version decodes to a non-nil pointer, verdict
31		// included. What the pointer adds is the case that was missing: a
32		// secrets stage cut off by the option or by a missing tool used to
33		// render `false`, i.e. "clean", for a scan that had not looked.

36		// is a pointer for exactly Sensitive's reason: nil means nobody graded this

38		// this context's forge, or the run was withheld. A letter is a claim, and
39		// an empty string in its place would be a fifth state nothing means.

42		// nil, which is the truth about it. ImageScanEntry gains nothing: an image

48	// WorkspaceScanCache manages workspace scan results cache.
49	//
50	// Bound to one configuration context, like ImageScanCache: workspaces_dir is
51	// per context, so two contexts legitimately hold different roots.
52	type WorkspaceScanCache struct {
53		mu       sync.RWMutex
54		path     string

59	// NewWorkspaceScanCache creates or loads the cache from
60	// ~/.devdesk/cache/workspace-scans.json, scoped to a configuration context.
61	func NewWorkspaceScanCache(context string) (*WorkspaceScanCache, error) {
62		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, err
65		}
66	
67		cacheDir := filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache")
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(cacheDir, 0755); err != nil {

76	// lookup, so tests can point at a temp file.

78		c := &WorkspaceScanCache{
79			path:     path,

88	func (c *WorkspaceScanCache) load() {

139	func (c *WorkspaceScanCache) Delete(repoPath string) error {

149		defer c.mu.Unlock()

151	}

153	// workspaceScanResultDir returns the directory for full scan results, creating it if needed
154	func workspaceScanResultDir() (string, error) {
155		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
156		if err != nil {
157			return "", err
158		}
159		dir := filepath.Join(homeDir, ".devdesk", "cache", "workspace-results")
160		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0755); err != nil {
161			return "", err
162		}
163		return dir, nil

166	// resultFilePath returns the JSON file path for the full scan result of a repo path.
167	// Uses SHA256 of the path to avoid invalid filename characters.
168	func resultFilePath(repoPath string) (string, error) {
169		dir, err := workspaceScanResultDir()
170		if err != nil {
171			return "", err
172		}
173		hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(repoPath))
174		filename := fmt.Sprintf("%x.json", hash)

178	// SaveWorkspaceScanResult persists a full scan result to disk.
179	// Designed to be called in a goroutine: go SaveWorkspaceScanResult(path, result)
180	func SaveWorkspaceScanResult(repoPath string, result *scan.Result) error {
181		filePath, err := resultFilePath(repoPath)
182		if err != nil {
183			return err
184		}
185		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(result, "", "  ")
186		if err != nil {

188		}
189		return os.WriteFile(filePath, data, 0600)
190	}

192	// StoreWorkspaceScan records one finished scan of a directory: the counts in the
193	// cache of the context the scan was launched in, and the full result beside it.
194	//
195	// The counts are scoped by context and the result is not — it is addressed by
196	// path, and a scan of /repos/devdesk is the same scan whichever context asked
197	// (see internal/cache/scan_context_test.go). Two callers write exactly this: the
198	// workspaces view for a repository, and the templates view for a template's
199	// materialized copy.
200	//
201	// A failure to save either half is logged and returned, but the entry is
202	// returned regardless: the scan happened, and its counts are what the caller
203	// reports.
204	func StoreWorkspaceScan(contextName, repoPath string, result *scan.Result) (WorkspaceScanEntry, error) {
205		entry := WorkspaceScanEntry{
206			RepoPath: repoPath,
207			Critical: result.Counts.Critical,
208			High:     result.Counts.High,
209			Medium:   result.Counts.Medium,
210			Low:      result.Counts.Low,
211			// The verdict comes from the scan and from nowhere else: a loop looking
212			// for "a finding whose Source is gitleaks" missed the secrets Trivy
213			// found, and could not tell that no stage had looked at all.
214			Sensitive: result.SecretVerdict(),
215			CIScore:   result.CIVerdict(),
216			ScannedAt: result.EndTime,
217		}
218	
219		var errs []error
220		if wc, err := NewWorkspaceScanCache(contextName); err != nil {
221			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("open cache: %w", err))
222		} else if err := wc.Set(repoPath, entry); err != nil {
223			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("cache set: %w", err))
224		}
225		if err := SaveWorkspaceScanResult(repoPath, result); err != nil {
226			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("save full result: %w", err))
227		}
228		return entry, errors.Join(errs...)
229	}

231	// DeleteWorkspaceScanResult removes the full scan result file from disk.
232	// Used by purgeScanCacheCmd before re-scanning to avoid stale results.
233	func DeleteWorkspaceScanResult(repoPath string) error {
234		filePath, err := resultFilePath(repoPath)
235		if err != nil {
236			return err
237		}
238		err = os.Remove(filePath)
239		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
240			return nil // already gone, not an error
241		}
242		return err
243	}

245	// LoadWorkspaceScanResult loads a full scan result from disk
246	func LoadWorkspaceScanResult(repoPath string) (*scan.Result, error) {
247		filePath, err := resultFilePath(repoPath)
248		if err != nil {
249			return nil, err
250		}
251		data, err := os.ReadFile(filePath)
252		if err != nil {
253			return nil, err
254		}
255		var result scan.Result
256		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &result); err != nil {
257			return nil, err
258		}
259		return &result, nil
260	}

Captain comme auteur.

## Security Scanning

**Where a scanner runs from is configured, not guessed.** `scan.trivy_source`,
`scan.gitleaks_source` and `scan.plumber_source` take `auto | binary | image`:

| Value | Resolution |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | the binary when there is one, the Docker image otherwise |
| `binary` | `trivy_path` when set, else the name on `PATH` — **fails rather than falling back to Docker** |
| `image` | `trivy_image`, even when a binary is installed |

`scan.CheckDependencies(cfg.Scan)` resolves the three tools and fills
`DependencyStatus`; `deps.TrivySpec()` / `GitleaksSpec()` / `PlumberSpec()`
hand a `ToolSpec`
(source + binary + image) to the command builders. `ToolSpec` replaced the
`(source ToolSource, image string)` pair those builders used to take — the pair
had nowhere to carry a configured path, which is why `trivy_path` sat unread
for so long (D27). Do not add a positional `binary` parameter back; put it on
the spec.

The loud failure on `binary` is deliberate: falling back to Docker is what made
the unread path invisible, because scans kept working with something other than
what was asked for.

`internal/scan/` orchestrates Trivy + Gitleaks:
- `scanner.go` — runs both tools concurrently, streams progress via `ProgressUpdate` channel
- `trivy.go` — CVE, secret, license, misconfiguration detection
- `gitleaks.go` — secrets detection with custom config support
- `category.go` — **where a finding goes: one rule, for everyone**

Here is the end-to-end map. Two gaps you'd copy by accident if you use plumber as the template are called out in 2c and 5.

## 1. `scan.Finding` and the Trivy decode structs

**`Finding`** (`internal/scan/scanner.go:99-159`) has these fields: `ID, Title, Description, Severity, Source, File, Line, Match, Fingerprint, PkgName, Version, FixedIn, Resolution, References, FixCommand, Class, Ecosystem, EndLine, Message, Status, Job, ScriptLine`. There is no field for the IaC dialect.

**Decode structs** (`internal/scan/trivy.go`):
- `TrivyResult` (17-25) has `Target, Class, Type`, plus Vulnerabilities, Secrets, Licenses and Misconfigurations.
- `TrivyMisconfiguration` (63-78) has `Type, ID, AVDID, Title, Desc, Message, Severity, Resolution, PrimaryURL, Status, CauseMetadata{StartLine, EndLine}`.

**`TrivyResult.Type` is dropped for misconfigurations.** It only reaches a Finding as `Ecosystem` on vulnerabilities (`trivy.go:178`). The misconfig loop (216-236) copies neither `result.Type` nor `misconf.Type`. It sets `ID: firstNonEmpty(AVDID, ID)` and `Source: "trivy-misconfig"`. `docs/backlog.md:14253-14261` (§3.80) records this exact gap.

## 2. How a tool is declared, detected and run

**Config.** `config.ScanConfig` is at `internal/config/config.go:327-372`:
- Per tool: `TrivySource/TrivyPath/TrivyImage`, `Gitleaks*`, `Plumber*` (auto | binary | image, constants at 317-323).
- Also: `UseTrivyServer/TrivyServer`, `Enable{Vuln,Secret,Misconfig,License}`, `EnableCIScore` (366), `PlumberConfig` (371).
- Empty source defaults to auto at 524-532. `Default()` is at 603-606.
- The "all toggles off" migration (558-562) must also check any new toggle, the way it checks `EnableCIScore`.
- Path expansion is at 830-834.

**`ScanOptions`** (`scanner.go:57-96`) is built only by `OptionsFromConfig` (`internal/scan/options.go:19-51`).

**Detection:**
- `DependencyStatus` (`scanner.go:325-352`) holds `<Tool>Available/Source/Version/Binary/Image` plus `EngineAvailable` and `ImageScanSocket`.
- Default images are at 371-375.
- `CheckDependencies` (385-437) calls `resolveTool(pref, path, name, image, engineAvailable, versionArgs...)` (`internal/scan/tool_source.go:70-109`). With `binary` it does not fall back to a container.
- `ToolSpec{Source, Binary, Image, HostSocket}` (`tool_source.go:19-34`) comes from `TrivySpec/GitleaksSpec/PlumberSpec` (38-53).

**Running:**
- `toolCmd{Name, Args, Env, Dir}` is at `internal/scan/run.go:21-41`. `String()` is used for logging and display.
- The `commandRunner` interface (82-88) is implemented by `cliRunner` (93-139). The swappable variable is `var runner` (173).
- A non-zero exit becomes `*exitError`, which carries the exit code.
- Container mode is `<engine> run --rm -v target:/scan:ro <image> ...`, with `containerScanPath="/scan"` (`trivy_args.go:17`). Examples: `wrapTrivy` (205-224) and `plumberArgs` (`plumber.go:82-119`).

**Orchestration.** `Scanner.Scan` (`scanner.go:545-736`) runs one errgroup goroutine per stage. Each stage:
- is gated on `options.EnableX && deps.XAvailable`;
- sends `ProgressUpdate{Stage, Label, Status}`;
- on failure calls `recordStageError` (237);
- otherwise appends findings under the mutex.

`missingToolErrors` (485-504) reports a missing tool. Plumber is not in it.

**Every file plumber touches:**
- **scan:**
  - `plumber.go` (args, exit codes, `RunPlumber`, `GetPlumberCommand`)
  - `plumber_parse.go`
  - `plumber_target.go` (`ciOptions`, per-target gating)
  - `category.go:28,40,55`
  - `scanner.go:74-81, 188-211, 221-227, 263, 307, 336-340, 374, 394-434, 617-652`
  - `tool_source.go:51-53`
  - `options.go:29-33`
  - `run.go:34-40` (the `Dir` field)
- **config:** `config.go:336-338, 358-371, 530, 552-559, 605, 834`
- **cache:** `internal/cache/workspace_scan.go:35-44, 215`
- **security UI:**
  - `findings.go:108, 145, 191-210` (tab and count)
  - `view.go:205-217` (tab label)
  - `header.go:248` (help text)
  - `inventory_table.go:276` (CI column)
  - `inventory.go:288`
  - `inventory_commands.go:45-48, 128, 146-160, 282, 315`
  - `model.go:154, 169`
  - `details.go:127`
  - `pipeline_source.go` and `pipeline_annotate.go` (tool-specific)
- **other UI:**
  - workspaces: `model.go:158`, `view.go:370-382, 588`
  - `internal/ui/theme/ciscore.go`
  - dashboard: `model.go:595-613`, `sections.go:976-985`
  - `internal/ui/configuration/fields.go:299-300, 333-341`
  - `internal/ui/templates/scan.go:165` (turns CI off for templates)
  - `internal/ui/about/view.go:177`
- **MCP:** nothing (see 5).
- **Docs:** `docs/architecture/scanning.md:91-200`, `configuration.md`, `templates.md`, `docs-site/docs/{explanation/scanning,reference/configuration}.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**2c. Gap 1: your configured plumber source/path/image is not used by real scans.** `NewScanner` (`scanner.go:461-468`) builds the `config.ScanConfig` it passes to `CheckDependencies` from Trivy and Gitleaks fields only. So a real scan resolves plumber with source auto, the PATH binary and the default image. Only the dashboard, which passes the full `cfg.Scan`, honours the plumber settings. Separately, `PlumberPath` is not `~`-expanded (`config.go:830-832`). A new tool must be added to both places.

## 3. Categories and the results tabs

**Categories.** The source constants are at `category.go:22-29`. The `Category` enum (36-41) is Vulnerability, Secret, License, Misconfiguration, CIScore. `Categorize` (47-60) switches on `Source` only; an unknown source counts as a vulnerability. `Result.CountFindings` (`scanner.go:249-269`) feeds `MisconfigCount` and `CIIssueCount`. `TotalFindings` is at 305.

**Tabs** (`internal/ui/security/findings.go`):
- Constants at 103-113: `TabCVE=0, TabSecrets, TabLicense, TabMisconfig=3, TabCIScore=4, TabRemediation=5, tabCount=6`.
- `tabCategory` map at 140-146; `filterFindingsByTab` at 149-165.
- `countFindingsByTab` (191-211) returns a fixed tuple of five counts.
- `switchTab` is at 223-230; tab/shift+tab cycling at 384/388.
- Labels are at `view.go:204-218`.
- The header's ctrl+o label changes on `TabMisconfig` (`header.go:69-72`).

**Columns.** The Misconfigurations tab uses the shared `findingColumns()` (`findings.go:39-68`), which is the same for every findings tab: Severity, ID, Title (search also matches PkgName and File), and Source (optional). `sourceDisplay` (172-187) maps `trivy-misconfig` to "misconfig". There is no File or Type column. The detail pane is `details.go:71-160`.

## 4. Remediation catalog and patch

**`internal/remediation/misconfig.go`:**
- `Rule{AVDID, Title, Fix func(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string)}` is at 27-41. `Fix` returns either edits or a decline reason.
- Reason constants are at 46-78.
- The `catalog` map (122-178) contains only Dockerfile rules (AVD-DS-0002, 0005, 0011, 0015, 0019, 0020, 0021, 0022, 0025, 0027, 0029).
- `FixFor` (184-190) applies only to `CategoryMisconfiguration`.
- `RuleKey` (198-212) normalises IDs: "AVD-DS-0002" and "DS002" both become "DS2". "KSV-0012" would become "KSV12".
- Every fixer rejects non-Dockerfiles through `dockerfile.IsDockerfileName(baseName(f.File))`, returning `ReasonNotADockerfile`.

**`internal/patch`:** `Span`/`Edit{Span, Old, New}` and `Rewrite`/`Diff` are in `rewrite.go:25-107`. It is byte-range only, not YAML-aware. `WriteIfUnchanged` is in `write.go:25`.

**UI hook.** `misconfig_write.go:80-140` gates on `TabMisconfig` and a directory target, then calls `FixFor`, `rule.Fix`, `patch.Rewrite` and `Diff`.

## 5. MCP `scan_result`

In `internal/mcp/scan_tools.go`:
- The `finding` projection (135-155) has `id, title, description, severity, category, source, file, line, end_line, message, status, fingerprint, pkg_name, version, fixed_in, class, ecosystem, resolution, references`. `Match` is left out on purpose; `Job`, `ScriptLine` and `FixCommand` are also not exposed.
- `expose()` (325-347) copies fields one by one, so a new Finding field (for example an IaC type) must be added there explicitly.
- `scanResultOut` (165-192) carries the severity counts, `secret_count`, `secrets_scanned`, `license_count`, `misconfig_count`, `errors`, `target_kind`, `root` and paging.

**5b. Gap 2: MCP has no CI category.** `categoryName` (357-368) has no case for `CategoryCIScore`, so plumber findings are reported as "vulnerability". `scanResultOut` also has no CI count or score. A new category has to be added here and in the jsonschema text at 140/160.

The MCP descriptions table is at `internal/mcp/tools.go:90-135`. The scan toggles are also shown in `context_tools.go:127-134`, which does not include CI.

## 6. Caches and verdicts

**Entries:**
- `WorkspaceScanEntry` (`internal/cache/workspace_scan.go:19-46`): Critical, High, Medium, Low, `Sensitive *bool`, `CIScore *string`, ScannedAt.
- `ImageScanEntry` (`internal/cache/image_scan.go:17-33`): the same without CIScore.
- Neither stores `MisconfigCount` or `LicenseCount`.

**Full results.** The whole `scan.Result` JSON is written to `~/.devdesk/cache/workspace-results/<sha256>.json` (`SaveWorkspaceScanResult`, 180-190). So any new `Finding` or `Result` field is persisted automatically; only the summary entries need new fields.

**Writers:**
- `StoreWorkspaceScan` (204-229), called from `workspaces/commands.go:200` and `templates/scan.go:152`
- `storeRescan` (`security/inventory_commands.go:292-320`)
- `oci_resources/commands.go:148`

**Verdict pattern.** `Result.SecretVerdict()` (`scanner.go:296`) and `CIVerdict()` (221-227) return nil when nothing looked, backed by the `SecretsScanned`/`CIScanned` flags. Use a pointer field with omitempty so older cache files decode as "unknown". The value also has to travel through `InventoryScanFinishedMsg` (`inventory_commands.go:37-51`) and into the MCP `scanTarget` (`scan_tools.go:31-41`).

## 7. Existing Kubernetes/Helm/Kustomize mentions in Go

There are almost none:
- `internal/ui/security/header.go:68`, a comment about not offering "Write Dockerfile" on a Kubernetes manifest.
- `header.go:248`, help text: "Dockerfiles, Terraform, K8s manifests (Trivy)".
- `internal/remediation/misconfig_test.go` mentions it in a test.

There is nothing for helm, kustomize, `Chart.yaml`, `kustomization.yaml`, kube-linter or Kyverno. The design discussion is backlog §3.80 (`docs/backlog.md:14221-14343`). It says Trivy already emits KSV-* rules, the missing piece is Type, and whether kube-linter, Kyverno or Kubescape add enough is an open question (row 4). §3.78 also discusses Kyverno and kube-linter (around 13981-13984).

## 8. `docs/architecture/scanning.md` (814 lines)

Headings: `## Security Scanning` (6), then `###` sections on what can be fixed (310), what a misconfiguration carries (337), the misconfig fix catalog (364), the Remediation tab (413) and writing the chosen bases (478). After that come `## The security inventory` (522), `## Scan Cache` (657), `## Who knows a scan is running` (736) and `## A scan can be stopped` (780).

There is no explicit "how to add a tool" section. The nearest guidance:
- Lines 8-31: `*_source` resolution, `CheckDependencies`, `XSpec()`, and "do not add a positional binary parameter; put it on the spec".
- Lines 91-200: the plumber write-up (per-target gating, exit codes, withheld verdict, how the column and tabs behave, `Dir`, token in the environment, config mount).
- Line 172: stage failures go to the log, not the screen.
- Line 202: `Categorize` is the only classifier.
- Line 213: `SecretVerdict` is the only verdict.

## 9. Configuration view

`internal/ui/configuration/fields.go:293-348`, "scan" page:
- A "Scanners" group of toggles (294-301).
- One group per tool: `cycle("<Tool> source", …, [auto, binary, image])`, `text("<Tool> binary")`, `text("<Tool> image", "Empty uses "+scan.Default<Tool>Image)`, and an optional `text("<Tool> config")`. Trivy is 302-316, Gitleaks 321-332, Plumber 333-342.
- Trivy server mode forces misconfig and license off (`configuration/update.go:347-353`).

The dashboard's tool list is in `dashboard/model.go:595-613` and `sections.go:976-985`. The comment there says the two lists must stay in sync.

## 10. Test conventions

- **Fake runner:** `scriptedRunner` plus `useRunner`, `answering` and `commandForStage` (`internal/scan/execute_test.go:20-90`). `byStage` and `stageOf` (`scan_test.go:27-67`) pick the stage by matching the command string, so a new tool needs its own case there.
- **Fixture deps:** `everyTool()` and `everyStage()` (`scan_test.go:71-91`) are passed to `newScannerWithDeps(opts, deps)`. Tests swapping the runner must not run in parallel.
- **Parsing:** Trivy JSON is inline in `parse_test.go` (e.g. `TestAMisconfigurationCarriesItsSpanMessageAndStatus`, 334). Plumber uses files in `internal/scan/testdata/plumber_complete.json` and `plumber_withheld.json`, loaded at `plumber_test.go:21`.
- **Other:** argument building is tested as pure functions (`command_test.go`, `plumber_test.go`), detection in `tool_source_test.go:158-184`, verdicts in `verdict_test.go`. Test names are sentences (`TestTheXDoesY`).
